```{r helper_func, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE}
add_footnotes <- function(tab, notes) {
  html <- paste0(
    "<p style='font-size:0.85em; line-height:1.4; margin-top:6px;'>",
    paste0("<sup>", seq_along(notes), "</sup>&nbsp;", notes, collapse = "<br/>"),
    "</p>"
  )
  tab$knitr         <- paste0(tab$knitr, html)
  tab$page.content  <- paste0(tab$page.content, html)
  tab$page.complete <- sub("</body>", paste0(html, "</body>"),
                           tab$page.complete, fixed = TRUE)
  tab
}

format_pval <- function(ps, html = FALSE) {
  ps_chr <- ps %>% round(digits = 3) %>% as.character()
  ps_chr[ps_chr == "0"] <- "< .001"
  ps_chr[ps_chr == "1"] <- "> .999" 
  ps_chr
}

format_model_table <- . %>%
  mutate(p.value = format_pval(p.value))

icc_3level <- function(y, data,
                       village = "c2_vil_clus_id",
                       group   = "c2_group25_uniqid",
                       covars  = NULL) {

  rhs <- c(covars, sprintf("(1 | %s/%s)", village, group))
  m   <- lme4::lmer(reformulate(rhs, response = y), data = data, REML = TRUE)

  grp_lab <- sprintf("%s:%s", group, village)   # lme4 labels nested terms inner:outer
  vc      <- as.data.frame(lme4::VarCorr(m))
  pick    <- function(g) {
    v <- vc$vcov[vc$grp == g]
    if (length(v) != 1L) stop("variance component not found: ", g)
    v
  }
  v_vil <- pick(village); v_grp <- pick(grp_lab); v_res <- pick("Residual")
  tot   <- v_vil + v_grp + v_res

  tibble::tibble(
    outcome     = y,
    N           = stats::nobs(m),
    n_village   = lme4::ngrps(m)[[village]],
    n_group     = lme4::ngrps(m)[[grp_lab]],
    var_village = v_vil,
    var_group   = v_grp,
    var_resid   = v_res,
    icc_village              = v_vil / tot,
    icc_group                = v_grp / tot,
    icc_same_group           = (v_vil + v_grp) / tot,
    icc_group_within_village = v_grp / (v_grp + v_res),
    singular                 = lme4::isSingular(m)
  )
}

z_on_ref <- function(x, ref) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  (x - mean(x[ref], na.rm = TRUE)) / sd(x[ref], na.rm = TRUE)
}

add_ref_z <- function(df, vars,
                      ref    = df$g_t == 0,   # reference group; override if needed
                      suffix = "_z") {

  vars <- as.character(vars)

  not_found <- setdiff(vars, names(df))
  if (length(not_found))
    stop("not found in data: ", paste(not_found, collapse = ", "))

  ref <- !is.na(ref) & ref                    # NA in the reference test -> excluded
  if (sum(ref) < 2L)
    stop("reference group has fewer than 2 rows")

  z_on_ref <- function(x) {
    x <- as.numeric(x)
    s <- stats::sd(x[ref], na.rm = TRUE)
    if (is.na(s) || s == 0) {
      warning("zero or undefined SD in reference group; returning NA")
      return(rep(NA_real_, length(x)))
    }
    (x - mean(x[ref], na.rm = TRUE)) / s
  }

  dplyr::mutate(df, dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(vars), z_on_ref,
                                  .names = paste0("{.col}", suffix)))
}

apa_num <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  s <- ifelse(is.na(x), "",
              sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), x))
  sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.", s)
}

std_to_ref <- function(x, ref, sign = 1) {
  m  <- mean(ref, na.rm = TRUE)
  s  <- sd(ref,   na.rm = TRUE)
  sign * (x - m) / s
}
```

# Balance Table at Baseline
```{r bsl_balance_check}
# Balance check across g_t = 0 vs g_t = 1 for the following baseline variables
# (all pulled from C2TB_stfu_wins). Continuous vars are summarized with
# Mean (SD) and compared with Welch's two-sample t; binary vars are
# summarized with Mean (SD) too (Mean = proportion) but compared with
# Pearson's chi-square on a 2 × 2 group-by-value table. Significance signs:
# *p < .05, **p < .01, ***p < .001.
#
# Variable list (test type indicated per user's outline):
#   bsl_hhh_age
#   refugee            (chi-square)
#   female_head        (chi-square)
#   someprimary_head   (chi-square)
#   somesecondary_head (chi-square)
#   hhsize
#   coh1_holdout       (chi-square)
#   dep
#   kessler_6_bsl
#   cantrils_bsl
#   bsl_fambus         (chi-square)
#   bsl_outhh_empl     (chi-square)
#   fcs_bsl

# ---- APA number formatter: 2 dp, drop leading zero (0.23 -> .23) ----
apa_num2 <- function(x, digits = 2) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), "",
         sub("^(-?)0\\.", "\\1.",
             sprintf(paste0("%.", digits, "f"), as.numeric(x))))
}

sig_star <- function(p) dplyr::case_when(
  is.na(p) ~ "",
  p < .001 ~ "***",
  p < .01  ~ "**",
  p < .05  ~ "*",
  TRUE     ~ ""
)

# ---- Cell wrappers for decimal alignment ----
# Each numeric value sits in a fixed-width right-aligned inline-block so
# decimals line up across rows. `t_cell` also reserves a 1.4em trailing
# block for sig signs (matches the regression tables' pattern).
n_cell <- function(n)
  paste0("<span style='display:inline-block;width:3em;text-align:right'>",
         format(n, big.mark = ","), "</span>")

msd_cell <- function(m, sd)
  # Wrap the whole "(SD)" in a right-aligned fixed-width span: this keeps
  # the parens tight around the number (padding goes to the LEFT of "(",
  # not between "(" and the digit) while still column-aligning the SD's
  # decimal point across rows, because the trailing ".dd)" is a constant
  # width.
  paste0(
    "<span style='display:inline-block;width:3.5em;text-align:right'>", m, "</span>",
    " ",
    "<span style='display:inline-block;width:4em;text-align:right'>(", sd, ")</span>"
  )

t_cell <- function(t, sig, test = "t") {
  # Prefix labels the test type (t = ... or χ² = ...). Prefix sits in a
  # tight right-aligned span so "=" lines up across rows; the number span
  # is only wide enough for the widest expected value ("-24.35" ≈ 2.6em),
  # so the number hugs "=" while its right edge stays fixed → decimals
  # column-align across rows.
  label <- if (identical(test, "chi")) "&chi;<sup>2</sup>" else "<i>t</i>"
  paste0(
    "<span style='display:inline-block;width:1.2em;text-align:right'>", label, "</span>",
    " = ",
    "<span style='display:inline-block;width:2.0em;text-align:right'>", t, "</span>",
    "<span style='display:inline-block;min-width:1.4em;text-align:left'>", sig, "</span>"
  )
}

# ---- Variables to summarize (test = "t" or "chi") ----
bal_vars <- tibble::tribble(
  ~var,                 ~label,                                    ~test,
  "bsl_hhh_age",        "Household head age",                      "t",
  "refugee",            "Refugee",                                 "chi",
  "female_head",        "Female-headed HH",                        "chi",
  "someprimary_head",   "HH head with some primary schooling",     "chi",
  "somesecondary_head", "HH head with some secondary schooling",   "chi",
  "hhsize",             "Household size",                          "t",
  "coh1_holdout",       "Cohort-1 holdout",                        "chi",
  "dep",                "Baseline: high distress (Kessler >= 5)",  "t",
  "kessler_6_bsl",      "Baseline: Kessler-6",                     "t",
  "cantrils_bsl",       "Baseline: global life satisfaction",      "t",
  "bsl_fambus",         "Baseline: HH owns business",              "chi",
  "bsl_outhh_empl",     "Baseline: HH member works for payment",   "chi",
  "fcs_bsl",            "Baseline: FCS",                           "t"
)

# ---- One row per variable ----
build_bal_row <- function(varname, label, test, df) {
  x <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(df[[varname]]))
  g <- df$g_t
  keep <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(g)
  x <- x[keep]; g <- g[keep]
  g0 <- x[g == 0]
  g1 <- x[g == 1]

  n0 <- length(g0); n1 <- length(g1)
  m0 <- if (n0 > 0) mean(g0) else NA_real_
  m1 <- if (n1 > 0) mean(g1) else NA_real_
  s0 <- if (n0 > 1) sd(g0)   else NA_real_
  s1 <- if (n1 > 1) sd(g1)   else NA_real_

  if (test == "chi") {
    ct <- suppressWarnings(tryCatch(
      stats::chisq.test(table(g, x)),
      error = function(e) NULL))
    stat <- if (is.null(ct)) NA_real_ else unname(ct$statistic)
    pval <- if (is.null(ct)) NA_real_ else ct$p.value
  } else {
    tt <- suppressWarnings(tryCatch(
      stats::t.test(g0, g1),
      error = function(e) NULL))
    stat <- if (is.null(tt)) NA_real_ else unname(tt$statistic)
    pval <- if (is.null(tt)) NA_real_ else tt$p.value
  }

  tibble::tibble(
    Variable = label,
    N0       = n_cell(n0),
    MSD0     = msd_cell(apa_num2(m0), apa_num2(s0)),
    N1       = n_cell(n1),
    MSD1     = msd_cell(apa_num2(m1), apa_num2(s1)),
    t        = t_cell(apa_num2(stat), sig_star(pval), test)
  )
}

bal_tab <- purrr::pmap_dfr(
  list(bal_vars$var, bal_vars$label, bal_vars$test),
  ~ build_bal_row(..1, ..2, ..3, C2TB_stfu_wins))

kableExtra::kbl(bal_tab,
                align     = "lccccc",
                col.names = c("Variable", "N", "M (SD)", "N", "M (SD)",
                              "t or &chi;<sup>2</sup> statistics"),
                escape    = FALSE) %>%
  kableExtra::add_header_above(
    c(" " = 1,
      "Control" = 2,
      "Group Therapy"    = 2,
      " " = 1),
    escape = FALSE
  ) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width        = FALSE,
                             bootstrap_options = c("hover", "condensed"))
```


# Psychological Distress

## Pooled Effect

### 3-month follow-up

Let's take a look at regression table first.

```{r psych_stfu_regtab}
psyInd_stfu_lm_rbst_fe <-
  lm_robust(psych_distress_index ~ g_t + kessler_6_bsl +
              female_head + someprimary_head +
              somesecondary_head + hhsize + coh1_holdout,
            fixed_effects = ~ c2_vil_clus_id,
            se_type = "HC1",
            data = C2TB_stfu_wins)

ksl10_stfu_lm_rbst_fe <-
  lm_robust(kessler_10 ~ g_t + kessler_6_bsl +
              female_head + someprimary_head +
              somesecondary_head + hhsize + coh1_holdout,
            fixed_effects = ~ c2_vil_clus_id,
            se_type = "HC1",
            data = C2TB_stfu_wins)

ksl6_stfu_lm_rbst_fe <-
  lm_robust(kessler_6 ~ g_t + kessler_6_bsl +
              female_head + someprimary_head +
              somesecondary_head + hhsize + coh1_holdout,
            fixed_effects = ~ c2_vil_clus_id,
            se_type = "HC1",
            data = C2TB_stfu_wins)


phq_stfu_lm_rbst_fe <-
  lm_robust(phq_total_score ~ g_t + kessler_6_bsl +
              female_head + someprimary_head +
              somesecondary_head + hhsize + coh1_holdout,
            fixed_effects = ~ c2_vil_clus_id,
            se_type = "HC1",
            data = C2TB_stfu_wins)

gad_stfu_lm_rbst_fe <-
  lm_robust(gad_total_score ~ g_t + kessler_6_bsl +
              female_head + someprimary_head +
              somesecondary_head + hhsize + coh1_holdout,
            fixed_effects = ~ c2_vil_clus_id,
            se_type = "HC1",
            data = C2TB_stfu_wins)

modelsummary(
  list(
    "Psychological distress index" = psyInd_stfu_lm_rbst_fe,
    "Kessler 10 total"             = ksl10_stfu_lm_rbst_fe,
    "Kessler 6"                    = ksl6_stfu_lm_rbst_fe,
    "PHQ total"                    = phq_stfu_lm_rbst_fe,
    "GAD total"                    = gad_stfu_lm_rbst_fe
  ),
  stars       = c(
    "<sup>†</sup>"   = 0.10,
    "*"   = 0.05,
    "**"  = 0.01,
    "***" = 0.001
  ),
  # Decimal alignment + column-centering recipe:
  #   * Each numeric cell is wrapped in an OUTER 5em-wide inline-block whose
  #     inner content is right-aligned.
  #   * Every cell ends with the SAME 1.4em trailing block (star for estimates;
  #     closing `)` for SEs; empty for N / R^2).
  #   * With the model columns center-aligned (`align = "lccccc"`), the outer
  #     block sits in the middle of each cell -> numbers look centered.
  #   * Because every outer block is exactly 5em wide with right-aligned inner
  #     content, every last digit lands at the same X-offset inside the block,
  #     so decimals line up across coefficients, SEs, N, and R^2.
  # Tune the outer `width:5em` up/down to control how much horizontal air sits
  # to the left of the numbers.
  estimate    = "<span style='display:inline-block;width:5em;text-align:right'>{estimate}<span style='display:inline-block;min-width:1.4em;text-align:left'>{stars}</span></span>",
  statistic   = "<span style='display:inline-block;width:5em;text-align:right'>({std.error}<span style='display:inline-block;min-width:1.4em;text-align:left'>)</span></span>",
  fmt         = apa_num,
  coef_omit   = "c2_vil_clus_id",
  coef_rename = c(
    "(Intercept)"        = "(Intercept)",
    "g_t"                = "group therapy",
    "kessler_6_bsl"      = "Baseline: Kessler-6",
    "female_head"        = "Female-headed HH",
    "someprimary_head"   = "HH head with some primary schooling",
    "somesecondary_head" = "HH head with some secondary schooling",
    "hhsize"             = "Household size",
    "coh1_holdout"       = "Cohort-1 holdout"
  ),
  # Same 5em outer wrapper + 1.4em trailing pad as the estimate/SE cells above
  # so N and R^2 sit in the same visual column as the coefficients and their
  # right-edges align.
  gof_map = list(
    list("raw" = "nobs",      "clean" = "N",
         "fmt" = function(x) paste0(
           "<span style='display:inline-block;width:5em;text-align:right'>",
           format(round(x)),
           "<span style='display:inline-block;min-width:1.4em'></span></span>")),
    list("raw" = "r.squared", "clean" = "R²",
         "fmt" = function(x) paste0(
           "<span style='display:inline-block;width:5em;text-align:right'>",
           apa_num(x),
           "<span style='display:inline-block;min-width:1.4em'></span></span>"))
  ),
  align  = "lccccc",   # label column left; 5 model columns centered (the fixed-width outer span keeps decimals aligned)
  title  = "Table 1. Effect of group therapy on psychological distress at 3m FU",
  notes  = c(
    "Numbers in parentheses are standard errors.",
    "Village is controlled as a fixed effect but not displayed in the table.",
    "Heteroskedasticity-consistent (HC1) standard errors."
  ),
  output = "html",
  escape = FALSE   # let raw HTML in `stars` (the <sup>…</sup> tags) render
)
```

Now let's look at the estimated means for each outcome variable for each condition.

#### Psychological distress index (`psych_distress_index`)
```{r psyInd_stfu}
psyInd_stfu_lm_rbst <-
  lm_robust(psych_distress_index ~ g_t +  kessler_6_bsl + 
              female_head + someprimary_head +
              somesecondary_head + hhsize + coh1_holdout + factor(c2_vil_clus_id),
            se_type = "HC1",
            data = C2TB_stfu_wins)

joint_tests(psyInd_stfu_lm_rbst)

psyInd_stfu_emm_rbst <-
  emmeans(psyInd_stfu_lm_rbst, ~ g_t, at = list(g_t = c(0, 1)))

summary(psyInd_stfu_emm_rbst, infer = TRUE) %>%
  format_model_table() %>%
  kable(digits = 3,
        col.names = c("GIPT", "est.", "SE", "df",
                      "lower CI", "upper CI", "t", "p")) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = TRUE)

contrast(psyInd_stfu_emm_rbst,
         method = list("GIPT - no GIPT" = c(-1, 1))) %>%
  summary(infer = TRUE) %>%
  format_model_table() %>%
  kable(digits = 3,
        col.names = c("GIPT", "est.", "SE", "df",
                      "lower CI", "upper CI", "t", "p")
        ) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = TRUE)
```

### 20-month follow-up


Let's take a look at regression table first.
```{r psych_enl_regtab}
psyInd_enl_lm_rbst_fe <-
  lm_robust(psych_distress_index ~ g_t + kessler_6_bsl + female_head +
              someprimary_head + somesecondary_head + hhsize + coh1_holdout,
            fixed_effects = ~ c2_vil_clus_id,
            se_type = "HC1",
```

Now let's look at the estimated means for each outcome variable for each condition.

#### Psychological distress index (`psych_distress_index`)
```{r psyInd_enl}
psyInd_enl_lm_rbst <-
  lm_robust(psych_distress_index ~ g_t +  kessler_6_bsl + female_head +
              someprimary_head + somesecondary_head + hhsize + coh1_holdout +
              factor(c2_vil_clus_id),
            se_type = "HC1",
            data = C2TB_enl_wins)

joint_tests(psyInd_enl_lm_rbst)

psyInd_enl_emm_rbst <-
  emmeans(psyInd_enl_lm_rbst, ~ g_t, at = list(g_t = c(0, 1)))

summary(psyInd_enl_emm_rbst, infer = TRUE) %>%
  format_model_table() %>%
  kable(digits = 3,
        col.names = c("GIPT", "est.", "SE", "df",
                      "lower CI", "upper CI", "t", "p")) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = TRUE)

contrast(psyInd_enl_emm_rbst,
         method = list("GIPT - no GIPT" = c(-1, 1))) %>%
  summary(infer = TRUE) %>%
  format_model_table() %>%
  kable(digits = 3,
        col.names = c("GIPT", "est.", "SE", "df",
                      "lower CI", "upper CI", "t", "p")
        ) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = TRUE)
```

Now let's look at the estimated means for each outcome variable for each condition.

##### Psychological distress index (`psych_distress_index`)
```{r psyInd_hst_enl}
psyInd_hst_enl_lm_rbst <-
  lm_robust(psych_distress_index ~ g_t +  kessler_6_bsl +
              female_head + someprimary_head +
              somesecondary_head + hhsize + coh1_holdout + factor(c2_vil_clus_id),
            se_type = "HC1",
            data = C2TB_enl_wins %>%
              filter(refugee == 0))

joint_tests(psyInd_hst_enl_lm_rbst)

psyInd_hst_enl_emm_rbst <-
  emmeans(psyInd_hst_enl_lm_rbst, ~ g_t, at = list(g_t = c(0, 1)))

summary(psyInd_hst_enl_emm_rbst, infer = TRUE) %>%
  format_model_table() %>%
  kable(digits = 3,
        col.names = c("GIPT", "est.", "SE", "df",
                      "lower CI", "upper CI", "t", "p")) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = TRUE)

contrast(psyInd_hst_enl_emm_rbst,
         method = list("GIPT - no GIPT" = c(-1, 1))) %>%
  summary(infer = TRUE) %>%
  format_model_table() %>%
  kable(digits = 3,
        col.names = c("GIPT", "est.", "SE", "df",
                      "lower CI", "upper CI", "t", "p")
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = TRUE)
```

##### Psychological distress index (`psych_distress_index`)
```{r psyInd_dep_hst_enl}
psyInd_dep_hst_enl_lm_rbst <-
  lm_robust(psych_distress_index ~ g_t*dep + kessler_6_bsl +
              female_head + someprimary_head +
              somesecondary_head + hhsize + coh1_holdout + factor(c2_vil_clus_id),
            se_type = "HC1",
            data = C2TB_enl_wins %>%
              filter(refugee == 0))

joint_tests(psyInd_dep_hst_enl_lm_rbst)

psyInd_dep_hst_enl_emm_rbst <-
  emmeans(psyInd_dep_hst_enl_lm_rbst, ~ g_t|dep,
          at = list(g_t = c(0, 1), dep = c(0,1)))

summary(psyInd_dep_hst_enl_emm_rbst, infer = TRUE) %>%
  format_model_table() %>%
  kable(digits = 3,
        col.names = c("GIPT", "depressed @ bsl", "est.", "SE", "df",
                      "lower CI", "upper CI", "t", "p")
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = TRUE)

contrast(psyInd_dep_hst_enl_emm_rbst,
         method = list("GIPT - no GIPT" = c(-1, 1))) %>%
  summary(infer = TRUE) %>%
  format_model_table() %>%
  kable(digits = 3,
        col.names = c("GIPT", "depressed @ bsl", "est.", "SE", "df",
                      "lower CI", "upper CI", "t", "p")
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = TRUE)
```

Now let's look at the estimated means for each outcome variable for each condition.

##### Psychological distress index (`psych_distress_index`)
```{r psyInd_ref_enl}
psyInd_ref_enl_lm_rbst <-
  lm_robust(psych_distress_index ~ g_t + kessler_6_bsl +
              female_head + someprimary_head +
              somesecondary_head + hhsize + coh1_holdout + factor(c2_vil_clus_id),
            se_type = "HC1",
            data = C2TB_enl_wins %>%
              filter(refugee == 1))

joint_tests(psyInd_ref_enl_lm_rbst)

psyInd_ref_enl_emm_rbst <-
  emmeans(psyInd_ref_enl_lm_rbst, ~ g_t, at = list(g_t = c(0, 1)))

summary(psyInd_ref_enl_emm_rbst, infer = TRUE) %>%
  format_model_table() %>%
  kable(digits = 3,
        col.names = c("GIPT", "est.", "SE", "df",
                      "lower CI", "upper CI", "t", "p")) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = TRUE)

contrast(psyInd_ref_enl_emm_rbst,
         method = list("GIPT - no GIPT" = c(-1, 1))) %>%
  summary(infer = TRUE) %>%
  format_model_table() %>%
  kable(digits = 3,
        col.names = c("GIPT", "est.", "SE", "df",
                      "lower CI", "upper CI", "t", "p")
        ) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = TRUE)
```

# Implementation Quality
## Therapy group dynamics
```{r gipt_feedback}
# Auto-detects every `gd_*` and `ipt_*` variable in the STFU dataset and
# builds a long-format frequency table (one row per observed response per
# question). Question wording and response wording come from the Stata
# variable label (`attr(x, "label")`) and value-label dictionary
# (`attr(x, "labels")`) that haven/rio preserve.
# -88 (Prefer not to answer) is kept as its own response row so it appears
# alongside the substantive responses; true NAs (question wasn't administered
# / respondent skipped) are excluded from the denominator so percentages sum
# to 100 within each question.

# Feedback variables live in the endline dataset — set both the discovery
# source AND the function body to the same frame so lookups don't miss.
feedback_data <- C2TB_enl_wins %>% filter(g_t == 1)
feedback_vars <-
  feedback_data %>%
  dplyr::select(starts_with("gd_"), starts_with("ip_")) %>%
  names()

build_feedback_rows <- function(var_name) {
  x_full   <- feedback_data[[var_name]]
  dep_full <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(feedback_data[["dep"]]))
  x_num  <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x_full))
  keep   <- !is.na(x_num)
  x_num  <- x_num[keep]
  dep_v  <- dep_full[keep]
  n_tot  <- length(x_num)
  if (n_tot == 0) return(NULL)

  qlab <- attr(x_full, "label")
  if (is.null(qlab) || nchar(qlab) == 0) qlab <- var_name

  vlabs <- attr(x_full, "labels")

  vals <- sort(unique(x_num))
  tab <- data.frame(
    value  = vals,
    n      = vapply(vals, function(v) sum(x_num == v),                          integer(1)),
    n_high = vapply(vals, function(v) sum(x_num == v & dep_v == 1, na.rm = TRUE), integer(1)),
    n_low  = vapply(vals, function(v) sum(x_num == v & dep_v == 0, na.rm = TRUE), integer(1)),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  if (!is.null(vlabs)) {
    vlabs_num      <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(unname(vlabs)))
    hit            <- match(tab$value, vlabs_num)
    tab$resp_label <- ifelse(is.na(hit),
                             as.character(tab$value),
                             names(vlabs)[hit])
  } else {
    tab$resp_label <- as.character(tab$value)
  }

  tab$pct <- 100 * tab$n / n_tot

  n_high_total <- sum(!is.na(dep_v) & dep_v == 1)
  n_low_total  <- sum(!is.na(dep_v) & dep_v == 0)

  tibble::tibble(
    variable     = var_name,
    n_total      = n_tot,
    n_high_total = n_high_total,
    n_low_total  = n_low_total,
    question     = qlab,
    response     = paste0(tab$resp_label, " (", tab$value, ")"),
    n            = tab$n,
    percent      = sprintf("%.1f%%", tab$pct),
    n_high       = tab$n_high,
    n_low        = tab$n_low
  )
}

feedback_long <- purrr::map_dfr(feedback_vars, build_feedback_rows)

if (nrow(feedback_long) == 0) {
  cat("No `gd_*` or `ip_*` variables with non-NA responses found in the selected dataset.")
} else {
  # Render with pack_rows: one section per variable. Body shows only
  # Response / N / % — variable name + question wording + total N sit in
  # each pack header. `pack_rows` is more robust on tibbles than
  # `collapse_rows` (which is what threw the earlier dimnames error).
  feedback_display <- feedback_long %>%
    dplyr::select(response, n, percent, n_high, n_low)

  kbl_out <- kableExtra::kbl(
    feedback_display,
    align     = "lrrrr",
    col.names = c("Response", "N", "%", "N (high distress)", "N (low distress)"),
    caption   = "GIPT participant feedback — response distribution at endline (N broken down by baseline distress status)"
  ) %>%
    kableExtra::kable_styling(
      full_width        = FALSE,
      bootstrap_options = c("hover", "condensed")
    )

  grp <- feedback_long %>%
    dplyr::mutate(.row = dplyr::row_number()) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(variable) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      start = min(.row),
      end   = max(.row),
      hdr   = paste0(dplyr::first(variable), " — ",
                     dplyr::first(question),
                     "  (N = ", dplyr::first(n_total),
                     "; high distress = ", dplyr::first(n_high_total),
                     ", low distress = ",  dplyr::first(n_low_total), ")"),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(grp))) {
    kbl_out <- kbl_out %>%
      kableExtra::pack_rows(grp$hdr[i], grp$start[i], grp$end[i])
  }

  kbl_out
}

kbl_out
```

## Social perception
```{r soc_perception}
# --- Raw tests ---
# Chi-square: bivariate association between baseline distress and each
# community-problem indicator.
chisq.test(table(C2TB_stfu_wins$dep, C2TB_stfu_wins$harassment))
chisq.test(table(C2TB_stfu_wins$dep, C2TB_stfu_wins$social_excluded))

# Logistic regression of each binary community-problem outcome on
# baseline distress (dep) × group therapy (g_t). The `dep * g_t`
# formula expands to main effects + interaction.
harassment_glm      <- glm(harassment      ~ dep * g_t,
                           family = binomial, data = C2TB_stfu_wins)
social_excluded_glm <- glm(social_excluded ~ dep * g_t,
                           family = binomial, data = C2TB_stfu_wins)
summary(harassment_glm)
summary(social_excluded_glm)


# --- Descriptive table ---
# Low (dep == 0) vs high (dep == 1) baseline distress.
# harassment / social_excluded / goals_challenges: from C2TB_stfu_wins (3m FU).
# seen_bygipt / seen_bygrpt:                       from C2TB_enl_wins  (20m FU).
# Cell format: statistic on line 1, "n = ###" on line 2.

fmt2 <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f", x)

# Proportion (%) of value == 1 by dep, plus cell N
prop_by_dep <- function(df, v) {
  d <- df[!is.na(df$dep) & !is.na(df[[v]]), , drop = FALSE]
  tibble::tibble(
    dep = c("0", "1"),
    n   = c(sum(d$dep == 0),                sum(d$dep == 1)),
    p   = c(mean(d[[v]][d$dep == 0]) * 100, mean(d[[v]][d$dep == 1]) * 100)
  )
}

# Mean (SD) by dep, plus cell N
mean_by_dep <- function(df, v) {
  d <- df[!is.na(df$dep) & !is.na(df[[v]]), , drop = FALSE]
  tibble::tibble(
    dep = c("0", "1"),
    n   = c(sum(d$dep == 0),          sum(d$dep == 1)),
    m   = c(mean(d[[v]][d$dep == 0]), mean(d[[v]][d$dep == 1])),
    s   = c(sd(d[[v]][d$dep == 0]),   sd(d[[v]][d$dep == 1]))
  )
}

# Two-line cell: statistic on line 1, "n = ###" on line 2 (smaller/dimmer)
n_line <- function(n)
  paste0("<br><span style='font-size:0.85em;color:#666'>n = ",
         format(n, big.mark = ","), "</span>")

cell_pct  <- function(row) paste0(fmt2(row$p), "%", n_line(row$n))
cell_mean <- function(row) paste0(fmt2(row$m), " (", fmt2(row$s), ")",
                                  n_line(row$n))

# ---- Compute the five variables ----
h  <- prop_by_dep(C2TB_stfu_wins, "harassment")
se <- prop_by_dep(C2TB_stfu_wins, "social_excluded")

r0 <- function(t) t[t$dep == "0", ]   # low-distress row
r1 <- function(t) t[t$dep == "1", ]   # high-distress row

soc_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
  Variable = c("Harassed",
               "Socially excluded"),
  Source   = c("3m FU", "3m FU"),
  low  = c(cell_pct(r0(h)),   cell_pct(r0(se))),
  high = c(cell_pct(r1(h)),   cell_pct(r1(se)))
)

kableExtra::kbl(soc_tbl,
                align     = "llcc",
                col.names = c("Variable", "Source",
                              "Low distress at baseline",
                              "High distress at baseline"),
                escape    = FALSE) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width        = FALSE,
                             bootstrap_options = c("hover", "condensed"))
```


# Joint Tables
```{r keyDV_reg}
# Reuses the 8 pooled *_lm_rbst_fe models defined earlier in this Rmd.
# `coef_map` fixes the predictor ORDER: g_t first, then each DV's matching
# baseline control (rows collapse: only the rows with data show a value
# for a given column), then the shared stratification covariates.
modelsummary(
  list(
    "Psych distress<br>(3m FU)"    = psyInd_stfu_lm_rbst_fe,
    "Psych well-being<br>(3m FU)"  = psyWB_stfu_lm_rbst_fe,
    "Econ activity<br>(3m FU)"     = econInd_stfu_lm_rbst_fe,
    "FCS<br>(3m FU)"               = fcs_stfu_lm_rbst_fe,
    "Psych distress<br>(20m FU)"   = psyInd_enl_lm_rbst_fe,
    "Psych well-being<br>(20m FU)" = psyWB_enl_lm_rbst_fe,
    "Econ activity<br>(20m FU)"    = econInd_enl_lm_rbst_fe,
    "FCS<br>(20m FU)"              = fcs_enl_lm_rbst_fe
  ),
  stars       = c(
    "<sup>&dagger;</sup>" = 0.10,
    "*"                   = 0.05,
    "**"                  = 0.01,
    "***"                 = 0.001
  ),
  estimate    = "<span style='display:inline-block;width:5em;text-align:right'>{estimate}<span style='display:inline-block;min-width:1.4em;text-align:left'>{stars}</span></span>",
  statistic   = "<span style='display:inline-block;width:5em;text-align:right'>({std.error}<span style='display:inline-block;min-width:1.4em;text-align:left'>)</span></span>",
  fmt         = apa_num,
  coef_omit   = "c2_vil_clus_id",
  coef_map = c(
    # 1. treatment
    "g_t"                = "Group therapy",
    # 2. per-DV baseline control (each row is non-empty only for the models that use it)
    "kessler_6_bsl"      = "Baseline: Kessler-6",
    "cantrils_bsl"       = "Baseline: global life satisfaction",
    "bsl_fambus"         = "Baseline: family owns business",
    "bsl_outhh_empl"     = "Baseline: HH member working for pay",
    "fcs_bsl"            = "Baseline: FCS",
    # 3. shared stratification covariates
    "female_head"        = "Female-headed HH",
    "someprimary_head"   = "HH head with some primary schooling",
    "somesecondary_head" = "HH head with some secondary schooling",
    "hhsize"             = "Household size",
    "coh1_holdout"       = "Cohort 1 holdout"
  ),
  gof_map = list(
    list("raw" = "nobs",      "clean" = "N",
         "fmt" = function(x) paste0(
           "<span style='display:inline-block;width:5em;text-align:right'>",
           format(round(x)),
           "<span style='display:inline-block;min-width:1.4em'></span></span>")),
    list("raw" = "r.squared", "clean" = "R²",
         "fmt" = function(x) paste0(
           "<span style='display:inline-block;width:5em;text-align:right'>",
           apa_num(x),
           "<span style='display:inline-block;min-width:1.4em'></span></span>"))
  ),
  align  = "lcccccccc",
  output = "html",
  escape = FALSE
)
```
